description: NaC₂PN₃H₅SO₄ crystallizes in the triclinic P̅1 space group. The structure is one-dimensional and consists of one NaC₂PN₃H₅SO₄ ribbon oriented in the (np.int64(0), np.int64(1), np.int64(0)) direction. Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share  a cornercorner with one PSN₂O tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.44-2.58 Å. There are two inequivalent C sites. In the first C site, C is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to two N and one O atom. There is one shorter (1.35 Å) and one longer (1.38 Å) C-N bond length. The C-O bond length is 1.26 Å. In the second C site, C is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to two N and one O atom. There is one shorter (1.36 Å) and one longer (1.38 Å) C-N bond length. The C-O bond length is 1.25 Å. P is bonded to two N, one S, and one O atom to form distorted PSN₂O tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There is one shorter (1.71 Å) and one longer (1.72 Å) P-N bond length. The P-S bond length is 1.95 Å. The P-O bond length is 1.53 Å. There are three inequivalent N sites. In the first N site, N is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one C, one P, and one H atom. The N-H bond length is 1.04 Å. In the second N site, N is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one C, one P, and one H atom. The N-H bond length is 1.04 Å. In the third N site, N is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to two C and one H atom. The N-H bond length is 1.04 Å. There are five inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one N atom. In the second H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one N atom. In the third H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one N and one O atom. The H-O bond length is 1.73 Å. In the fourth H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one O atom. The H-O bond length is 0.98 Å. In the fifth H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one O atom. The H-O bond length is 1.00 Å. S is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one P atom. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted water-like geometry to one Na and two H atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one C, and one H atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na and one C atom.
